html: The Jiwarli, also spelt Djiwarli, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Pilbara region of Western Australia, in the country of the Henry River, a branch of the Ashburton. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Their neighbours included the Jurruru, Thiin and Pinikura to the north and east and the Warriyangga to the south. The last fluent speaker of the Jiwarli language, Jack Butler, died in 1986; the linguist Peter Austin recorded his stories and published a grammar and dictionary of the language.
